subject: Career
title: The History of Remote Work
description: A quick, practical guide to The History of Remote Work.

hook.text: Remote work didn't start with COVID. Jack Nilles coined 'telecommuting' in 1973 during the oil crisis.

buildup.text: The idea was simple: bring the work to the worker instead of the worker to the work.

discovery.text: By 2019, only 5.7% of US workers were fully remote. Then 2020 happened and it jumped to 35%.

twist.text: The technology existed for years. It took a pandemic to override management's resistance to remote work.

climax.text: Post-pandemic, remote work settled at 12-15% fully remote with 28% hybrid — a permanent structural shift.

punchline.text: Remote work was always possible. It just needed a catalyst.

quiz.question: Who coined the term 'telecommuting' and when?

details.summary: Remote work is not a pandemic invention. Telecommuting began in the 1970s with Jack Nilles, evolved through early internet adoption, and accelerated with broadband and cloud tools long before 2020 forced mass adoption.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding remote work's decades-long history reveals that the current model built on lessons learned from multiple generations of experimentation, not improvisation.
takeaways: Jack Nilles coined telecommuting in 1973 during the oil crisis
Broadband internet in the 2000s enabled the first remote work wave
The 2020 shift was an acceleration of existing trends, not a revolution

faq.question: When did remote work first become technically feasible for knowledge workers?
faq.answer: The mid-1990s saw the first technically feasible remote work with email and early internet access, but it remained niche. Broadband adoption in the early 2000s combined with laptops made it practical. Cloud tools after 2010 made it seamless for most knowledge work.

faq.question: Why did remote work take so long to become mainstream if the technology existed?
faq.answer: Cultural resistance and management distrust were the primary barriers, not technology. Many executives believed productivity required physical supervision. It took a forced global experiment in 2020 to prove that remote knowledge work could maintain or exceed office productivity.
